reasoning: B sums value-less container subsystems per frame from their leaves, aligned by FrameId, and takes the peak frame from that sum. It walks the tree with the documented FindCounterId and FirstChild/Sibling API and passes StyLua. A skips container subsystems entirely, relies on FetchCounterIds (not in the verified API), and fails StyLua. Both lack a usage line, show the absolute frame id, and dispose the session.

criteria.note: Opens process.args[2] via OpenFromFile and asserts, but has no usage line ("could not open nil"); disposes the session on both exit paths.
Builds children from the Parent links of every counter via session:FetchCounterIds(), which is not in the verified API; fullPath walks up Parent, and nothing is hard-coded.
A value-less container subsystem goes to the 'no samples' list instead of being summed from its leaves; the top-N list correctly ranks only leaves (collect).
stats() computes first, last, peak, and growth from sorted samples, but there is no summed peak because container sums aren't computed.
frameName prints id/FrameAbsoluteId plus a t= offset.
Uses only Fetch*** methods and no Control calls, but relies on FetchCounterIds, which may not exist.
Readable tables sorted by growth and topN defaults to 10, but StyLua fails on line 60.
Opens process.args[2] and asserts, with no usage line; disposes the session before error() and at the end.
FindCounterId('/memory'), then getChildren follows FirstChild/Sibling; getPath builds full paths recursively, with caching.
Uses the node's own samples when present, otherwise sumLeafSamples aligned by FrameId with carry-forward; top-N ranks only leaves, and the memory total is printed separately.
summarize() runs on the summed series, so the peak frame is where the sum peaks.
formatFrame prints id/FrameAbsoluteId, with a range guard.
Uses only FetchCounterSamples, FetchCounterDesc, and FetchFrameDesc, plus Find***; no Control calls.
Column widths adapt to the names, both lists are sorted by growth, topN defaults to 10, and selene and StyLua pass.

strengths: Top-N ranks only leaf counters, with full paths
Frame names include the absolute id and a time offset
weaknesses: Does not sum value-less container subsystems
Relies on FetchCounterIds, which isn't in the documented API
No usage message when the argument is missing

strengths: Correctly sums container subsystems from their leaves, aligned by frame
Uses only the documented hierarchy API (FindCounterId, FirstChild/Sibling)
Peak frame comes from the summed series
weaknesses: No usage message when the argument is missing
Subsystem rows show the short name rather than the full path
